records.english: {SPEAKER:06}Never mind the fool. Now that that's settled, let's gather what you'll need for the voyage.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio ends the argument and turns everyone's attention to preparing for the voyage.
records.source_meaning: Julio says to ignore the fool; since the decision is made, good preparation matters, so they should gather the voyage supplies.
records.localization_note: The Japanese preparation proverb is localized by stating its practical intent instead of translating it literally.

records.english: {SPEAKER:06}This is hard work, so stay close.{PAD}
records.speaker: Julio Erneco
records.context: Julio warns Raphael that the preparations will be demanding and tells him to follow carefully.
records.source_meaning: Julio says the preparations will be difficult and tells Raphael to keep up with him.
records.localization_note: Natural spoken instruction replaces the literal request to follow firmly.

records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael eagerly asks Julio to teach him how to prepare for the voyage.
records.source_meaning: Raphael eagerly asks Julio to teach him.
records.localization_note: The enthusiastic request is already idiomatic in American English.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Tch. Knowing ships doesn't mean he can teach {MACRO:FI}.{PAD}
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio grumbles that Julio is acting like Raphael's teacher just because he knows about ships.
records.source_meaning: Claudio complains that Julio knows a little about ships and is already acting like Raphael's teacher.
records.localization_note: The insult is kept conversational, and the protagonist macro remains intact.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus cuts off Claudio's grumbling and gets the group moving.
records.source_meaning: Janus tells Claudio to stop mouthing off and says they should go.
records.localization_note: Backtalk matches Janus's corrective tone without preserving Japanese repetition.

records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus announces that it is time to begin the voyage preparations.
records.source_meaning: Janus says they should begin the preparations needed for the voyage.
records.localization_note: Get ready to sail is the natural concise American equivalent.

records.english: {SPEAKER:04}Will Julio show you the ropes, or will you prepare on your own?{PAD}
records.speaker: Janus Pasar
records.context: Janus asks whether Raphael wants Julio's guided tutorial or prefers to prepare independently.
records.source_meaning: Janus asks whether Raphael will learn the preparations from Julio or prepare to depart by himself.
records.localization_note: Show you the ropes is a natural nautical localization that preserves the tutorial-versus-independent choice.
